notes:
Three real rungs: apply to Darcia, attune the device at any ONE Geomagnetic Fount, come back. The interesting decision is evidence, and the answer is none. The [KI] Geomagnetron is handed over at bullet 1, mid-mission, and would be a textbook step-1 evidence point -- except that it also sits in the header Reward alongside the [KI] Adoulinian charter permit, and hard rule 7 says a header reward proves the mission is over, not that a step is done. I am recording the tension rather than picking a side quietly: the cost of obeying the rule here is that nothing advances the ladder, so the mark stays on Darcia while the player is actually underground. If a human ever revisits this record, THAT is the line to argue about. The Geomagnetron does appear in steps 2 and 3 as `items`, which is the legal way to say you must be carrying it -- exactly the split the brief draws for the ToAU supplies package.

Step 2 is an eighteen-way OR, not a sequence and not a group: you attune ONE fount and the mission is satisfied. A group would mean all eighteen, and eighteen separate rungs would mark a player who went to Gusgen as if she were owed Garlaige. So it is one step with `zone` deliberately null, which lets the row match the Geomagnetic Fount in whichever dungeon the player actually chose; the full list with grids is in the step note.

Bullet 4 is not a step -- it is two ways to SKIP the mission (1,000,000 gil to Darcia, or having done Rhapsodies of Vanadiel 'The River Runs Red', after which Iroha hands you the device). The 'Suggestions For New Players' section after the walkthrough is route advice and map links for three of the eighteen founts, not further steps.

notes:
Only bullet 3 is a step. Bullet 1 is not an instruction at all -- it is a note about how the fame level trades off against imprimaturs spent, with the wiki's own figure of 15 imprimaturs plus the 'I'm on a Boat' and 'Hide and Go Peak' quests being enough. Bullet 2 is an outcome ('you also gain the ability to purchase' the Wildskeeper Reive key items, from Dimmian in Eastern Adoulin (E-6)), not something you do.

So the actual body of this mission -- run coalition assignments until you have burned enough imprimaturs -- has no bullet, no observable and no marker: nothing in the packets counts imprimaturs or coalition work. That is a real gate the ladder cannot express, which is what medium confidence is for; the ladder itself (talk to Brenton) is right. Demoted rather than flagged-and-left-high because a player standing in front of Brenton too early will get nothing and the mark cannot tell her why.

The [KI] Dinner invitation is the header Reward and marks the mission's end, so it is not evidence.

The page says to read all three options in the book entitled History on the bookshelf, and locates the section between Yefafa and Vainrachault -- both of whom are library NPCs standing nearby, not the thing you click. It is not recorded as `items` because the page attaches the card to starting Order Up rather than to this step. Empty Reward and nothing handed over, so no evidence.

Bullet 1 is pure routing -- its own sub-bullet says so, '(This is the fastest route to talk to Chalvava.)' -- so it merges into the Chalvava step rather than becoming a travel rung of its own; a rung whose only content is 'go in by the nearer door' is noise.

notes:
The best-observed mission in this lane: a fetch of four key items, none of them in the header Reward (which is empty), each granted at its own distinct step, so all four steps carry real evidence and the ladder actually walks. That is four separate items on four separate rungs, so the no-duplicate-evidence rule is respected without effort.

Header Start is empty; the first bullet names Ploh Trishbahk (K-9) in Eastern Adoulin, agreeing with chronicle_snpc ('ploh trishbahk').

Ordering follows the page exactly and it is not a straight line. Rigobertine is strictly first of the four -- 'You cannot obtain the other items without this cutscene' -- and Erminold is strictly last, because bullet 5's sub-bullet says the weather vane wings always come last and need both of the others. What sits between is genuinely unordered: Fontis Xanira and the Sunrise Beacon 'can be obtained in either order', so they share a group and both draw at once instead of the ladder insisting on one.

Bullet 6 is not a step. 'After obtaining the 4 Key Items you will be on the next Mission' is the mission ending, not something you do, and there is no hand-in NPC at all -- do not expect one.

Grids: Fontis Xanira is recorded as H-8/9 because the page puts the fountain on the border and refuses to pick, which is the page's own wording rather than a conflict.
